check: whether the s0 evidence families share the ambiguity fixed in the fault-matrix and wall-run families
why: Two families needed labelling because a reader could not tell which directories were results. Three more had not been examined, and the fastest way to know whether a family needs a note is to look at its names.

s0Families.s0_02: 3 subdirectories (adapter, matrix, runtime) and 6 top-level files
s0Families.s0_03: 6 subdirectories (adapter, junit, matrix, recovery, regression, runtime) and 19 top-level files
s0Families.structure: Organised by category rather than as a flat list of runs, so the directory a reader opens already says what kind of evidence it holds.

theLargestFamilyIsSelfLabelling.namingPattern: s002-<mods>-<concurrency>-<outcome>-<8 hex chars>, for example s002-tectonic-c2me-1-success-2a07484c
theLargestFamilyIsSelfLabelling.whatTheNameCarries: The profile under test, the concurrency, the outcome, and a unique suffix
theLargestFamilyIsSelfLabelling.outcomeDistribution: 66 success, 12 fail, 9 cancel - parsed from the names themselves, with no directory lacking an outcome marker
theLargestFamilyIsSelfLabelling.verdict: A reader can tell result from non-result by reading the directory name, which is exactly what the fault-matrix and wall-run families could not do.

whyTheseNeedNoNote: The two families that needed labelling had ambiguous names - a timestamp and a hash - and mixed outcomes inside. These name their outcome, so the ambiguity never arises. Adding a README here would restate what the names already say.
whatThisConfirms: The problem was never that multiple directories exist; it was that some families do not say which is which. Naming is the cheaper fix, and s0-02/matrix is the example of it done well.
